rationale: Fourth turn: converted the locally reproduced failure into a fixed-input experiment. draft/assurance_generated.rs is a deterministic, single-threaded, in-process harness for the omnipaxos package (three real OmniPaxos instances, explicit tick/route steps, one instance recreated from its persisted storage). It drives the case to the state the souried analysis predicts is decisive, asserts the prefix conditions, and reports the outcome as a CA_EVENT. The same harness was run locally first (test completes, outcome event aborts with 'attempt to subtract with overflow'); the request now asks the controller to run it as retained evidence so the conclusion can move from a conditional/unresolved account to an asserted defect.

scope.description: Three-node in-process cluster of real OmniPaxos instances driven by explicit tick and route steps; one node is recreated from its persisted storage to model crash-recovery, one node's incoming decision traffic is dropped, the leader trims the decided prefix, the leader is then removed, and the recovered node performs a takeover.
assumptions: Node pids {1,2,3}, configuration_id 1, majority quorum, batch_size 3, election/resend tick timeouts 2/4, flush_batch_tick_timeout 1000 (deliberately long so batching is driven by fills and decisions).

Entry type has Snapshots disabled (T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() == false), as the harness defines it; storage is the captured MemoryStorage behind a shared handle so the crashed node recovers the exact durable state it had written.

Lost traffic is modelled as dropping whole messages addressed to one node (Decide/AcceptDecide traffic while it must stay at decided 3, then AcceptSync after it must promise without accepting); nothing is corrupted and no node is Byzantine.
Dev profile, i.e. overflow checks enabled, matching the controller's cargo test invocation.
excluded: Release-profile behaviour (overflow checks disabled) is not measured by this experiment.
PersistentStorage/RocksDB, snapshot-capable entry types, unicache and the async actor layer are not exercised here.
Crash of the operating-system process, and any storage-medium fault.

experiment.prefix: Cluster::new(3, 3) builds three OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2,3) over shared MemoryStorage handles, then pump_until(2000) ticks/routes until a leader (Leader, Accept) exists; three entries 0,1,2 are appended on that leader and pump_until(4000) waits until every node reports decided_idx == 3. followers are sorted and the two non-leaders are named v (stale node) and f (healthy follower). Three more entries 10,11,12 are appended on the leader; the driver then routes message by message and inserts v into the mute set the moment get_accepted_idx(v) == 6, so v accepts all six entries while the decision-bearing traffic is dropped for it, while f is allowed to reach decided_idx == 6. The leader then calls trim(Some(6)) (every node has accepted 6, so the trim is legal), the driver waits until get_compacted_idx(f) == 6 (the forwarded Compaction::Trim is delivered to f and the crashed-so-far v is muted so it misses it). The driver then removes the leader from the cluster (crash), unmutes v, and drops only AcceptSync addressed to v so v can promise to the replacement leader without accepting under its ballot; pump_until(4000) waits until f reports get_current_leader() == Some((f, true)). Finally the driver calls v.try_become_leader(), which makes v send Prepare{n: v's promise + 1, decided_idx: 3, n_accepted: r1, accepted_idx: 6} to its peers, and a single route() step delivers that Prepare to f inside catch_unwind; the resulting outcome (completed vs aborted panic, plus panic message and the observed index fields) is printed as a CA_EVENT.
semantic_changes: No harness helper replaces production logic; the cluster drives the captured crate's public API (append, tick, take_outgoing_messages, handle_incoming, trim, try_become_leader, get_decided_idx, get_accepted_idx, get_compacted_idx, get_current_leader, get_promise).
experiment.responsibility: Two captured components participate: the core's follower Prepare handling chooses its log-update prefix (the preparing leader's decided_idx) without comparing it to the responder's own compacted index, and the captured in-memory storage implementation computes get_suffix(from) with an unchecked subtraction that panics for from < trimmed_idx although the Storage trait it implements specifies returning an empty vector when entries do not exist for the complete interval.

comparisons.description: The healthy follower that has compacted to 6 handles the Prepare of a node whose decided index is 3 and whose accepted index is 6 without aborting.
The outcome event is emitted while the responder's compacted index is still 6, i.e. the observed update request is below its compacted prefix.

knowledge.assertion: with snapshots disabled the log update is built as get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) with no comparison against the responder's own compacted index
MemoryStorage::get_suffix(from) subtracts trimmed_idx unchecked and panics with overflow checks enabled for from < trimmed_idx
